name: Korah
overview: Korah was a male chief of Edom and son of Eliphaz, belonging to the Edomite tribe. His leadership role is noted specifically in Genesis 36:15-16. Beyond his tribal affiliation and leadership, no additional personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Korah means 'shaven' or 'bald' in Hebrew, as recorded in Genesis 36:16. This is the only name attributed to him and no divine naming is indicated.
familyAndRelationships: Korah is explicitly identified as the son of Eliphaz, establishing a direct familial link within the Edomite lineage. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Korah's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as a leader who challenged God's appointed authority, specifically against Moses and Aaron. His rebellion, alongside others, resulted in divine judgment that affirmed God's chosen leadership and priesthood. This episode serves as a solemn reminder of the consequences of opposing God's established order.

keyEvents.event: Led rebellion against Moses and Aaron
